content: I have statred working on iris/program_logic/weakestpre.v, which also includes bi/weakestpre.v for the notation and typeclasses

About this topic, I had a couple of questions:

  1. How relevant is stuckness really? I see it all over the place, but I don't know many people that use it. Maybe I just don't know enough people
  2. Do we wan to keep the WP notation the same as in Rocq? In particular, I was wondering whether to do something closer to what Std.Do.WP is doing notation-wise, where they write wp⟦e⟧ φ vs wp e {{ φ }}

For 1:
I was also wondering about why stuckness is there at some point. Here are the relevant discussion I found before:
The stuckness was introduced in Iris 3.1.0, which is used in the OOPSLA'17 paper mentioned in the CHANGLOG:
https://gitlab.mpi-sws.org/iris/iris/-/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#iris-310-released-2017-12-19

And this: https://mattermost.mpi-sws.org/iris/pl/f84p4fkxsjrnmqwn3nurph178c

I don't know any project besides the OOPSLA'17 paper that uses MaybeStuck

I used stuckness in my first POPL paper (which was based on the OCPL paper). But I don't think it is very widely used otherwise. However, being able to put some other parameter in the notation of WP is used by a bunch of projects so preserving the ability to do that would be quite useful.

Fernando LEAL said:

  1. Do we wan to keep the WP notation the same as in Rocq? In particular, I was wondering whether to do something closer to what Std.Do.WP is doing notation-wise, where they write wp⟦e⟧ φ vs wp e {{ φ }}

For this it would probably best to get a range of opinions from different people. I personally prefer the Rocq notation.
I also prefer the Rocq notation. Not clashing with Std.Do is actually a good thing I think.
